phases.name: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
phases.description: Keep the live brief intact, distinguish a supported hypothesis from a proven cause, and expose measurement details the prompt leaves open.

phases.name: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
phases.description: Bring metrics, logs, traces, and deployment changes through a durable processing path while preserving source evidence and maintaining the dependency graph.

phases.name: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
phases.description: Connect automatic investigation triggers and operator requests to evidence stores, causal ranking, and a reviewable case record.

phases.name: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
phases.description: Close the feedback loop through offline evaluation and model versioning, then test only against the scale and quality targets in the prompt.

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Freeze the live problem brief
steps.content:
Title: Design an Automated Root Cause Analysis Platform
Description: Design a platform that automatically identifies root causes of production issues by analyzing metrics, logs, traces, and topology, reducing mean time to resolution significantly.
Requirements:
- Correlate metrics, logs, and traces for root cause
- Build and maintain service dependency graphs
- Identify causal chains from symptom to root cause
- Analyze deployment changes as potential causes
- Score and rank probable root causes
- Provide evidence and reasoning for each hypothesis
- Learn from operator feedback on correctness
- Integrate with monitoring and deployment systems
Constraints:
- Root cause identification within 5 minutes
- Accuracy above 80% for top-3 suggested causes
- Handle 100+ services with 1000+ metrics each
- Process 1TB+ of observability data daily
- Support both infrastructure and application issues
Hints:
- Use causal inference models (PC algorithm, Granger causality)
- Implement graph-based propagation analysis
- Use anomaly detection across correlated time-series
- Implement change correlation with deployment events
- Use distributed tracing for request-level analysis
- Implement knowledge graphs for historical cause patterns

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Pin down what the five-minute target measures
steps.content: The prompt sets root cause identification within 5 minutes but does not define the clock start or stop. Ask whether timing begins when an issue is first detected, when the platform has enough evidence to open an investigation, or when an operator requests one; stop at a ranked, evidence-backed result. Keep that definition explicit in evaluation rather than quietly substituting a component latency.

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Make the top-three accuracy claim reviewable
steps.content: The stated quality target is accuracy above 80% for top-3 suggested causes. Agree how a reviewed incident establishes its cause, how ambiguous or multi-cause incidents are labeled, and which evaluated suggestions count as correct. The prompt does not specify a dataset, denominator, or evaluation window; leave those as explicit evaluation decisions and do not claim the target from architecture alone.

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Treat each signal as evidence with its own provenance
steps.content: Metrics, logs, and traces have different payloads and clocks. Preserve the source, original event time, service identity when supplied, and a reference to the underlying evidence so a later hypothesis can be checked against the signal that supported it. Do not reduce the investigation to a single correlation score.

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Separate correlation from a causal explanation
steps.content: A nearby metric spike or deployment is a candidate explanation, not proof. A useful hypothesis should connect the observed symptom to a plausible upstream cause through service dependencies and signal evidence, and should show what supports or weakens that path. Keep the distinction visible to the operator.

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Use only the scale stated in the prompt
steps.content: The supplied workload is 100+ services with 1000+ metrics each and 1TB+ of observability data daily. Do not turn those lower bounds into an assumed event rate, burst multiplier, retention period, or per-service distribution. Measure the actual payload sizes, arrival patterns, and skew when validating capacity.

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Keep infrastructure and application investigations in scope
steps.content: The platform must support both infrastructure and application issues. Carry enough source and service context through the same evidence path to investigate either class, while letting the dependency graph and observed signals determine the relevant path for a particular case.

steps.phase: 1. Define the diagnosis contract
steps.title: Keep integration and learning boundaries explicit
steps.content: Monitoring and deployment systems are inputs to the platform; operator corrections are feedback about a result. Keep those external integrations separate from the platform's own model training and case history so a source outage or an unreviewed correction cannot silently become a new cause label.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Connect the metrics source
steps.content: Represent the monitoring integration that supplies service metrics and alerts. Keep the source integration configurable because the prompt names no monitoring vendor or metric format.

component.label: Metrics & Monitoring Source
component.description: Monitoring integration supplying metric and alert evidence

properties.purpose: Integrate with existing monitoring systems to ingest metrics and alert evidence for both infrastructure and application investigations without assuming a vendor, metric schema, or collection interval.

component.highlightReason: Metrics are one of the explicitly required evidence sources and monitoring integration is named in the prompt.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Connect the log processing source
steps.content: Use the existing log-processing catalog component for log intake and retrieval. Keep indexing and parsing behavior aligned to available source formats; the problem does not prescribe a log product or retention duration.

component.label: Log Processing & Evidence Index
component.description: Log intake, processing, and evidence retrieval

properties.purpose: Integrate the existing application and infrastructure log sources, process records for investigation, and retrieve relevant evidence while preserving source references; the problem specifies neither a vendor nor a retention period.

component.highlightReason: Logs are an explicit root-cause evidence source; the catalog already has a log-processing component.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Add the missing distributed-trace integration
steps.content: The component catalog has no dedicated distributed-tracing integration. Use its existing generic custom component for this concrete gap, keeping the payload limited to trace evidence and its source references; do not introduce a new catalog type.

component.label: Distributed Trace Adapter
component.description: Generic catalog component representing the trace-source integration gap

properties.purpose: Adapt distributed trace records from the existing tracing source into the evidence pipeline, preserving trace and span references and the source-provided service context. The component catalog has no dedicated distributed-tracing integration, so this uses the existing generic custom component for that gap.

component.highlightReason: Distributed tracing is required by the prompt and has no dedicated component in the existing catalog.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Connect deployment change events
steps.content: Represent the existing deployment system as the source of change events. Preserve the change identity and event time supplied by that system so a deployment can be considered as a possible cause without treating temporal proximity as proof.

component.label: Deployment & Change Events

properties.purpose: Integrate with deployment systems and emit source-provided change events with their identity and timing so investigations can compare changes with symptoms without assuming a deployment caused them.

component.highlightReason: Deployment changes are an explicit candidate cause and the prompt requires deployment-system integration.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Create a durable evidence intake boundary
steps.content: Buffer evidence from each source before correlation so a temporarily slow processor does not require every monitoring, logging, tracing, and deployment integration to synchronously run an investigation.

component.label: Durable Evidence Event Bus
component.description: Buffers source events for asynchronous correlation and replay

properties.purpose: Buffer metrics, logs, traces, and deployment-change references for asynchronous processing and replay while preserving source identity and event provenance.

component.highlightReason: A durable boundary decouples the four source integrations from correlation and protects evidence during downstream delays.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Route metrics into durable intake
steps.content: Accept metric and alert events from the monitoring integration without requiring it to call the causal analysis path synchronously.

connection.label: Metric and alert evidence
connection.description: Monitoring events enter the durable evidence stream with source references and source-provided event times.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Route logs into durable intake
steps.content: Send log evidence or references through the same durable boundary, keeping access to the original record for later explanation.

connection.label: Log events and evidence references
connection.description: Log processing publishes searchable evidence references and source event context for correlation.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Route trace context into durable intake
steps.content: Preserve trace and span references as evidence links rather than copying a trace into an opaque summary.

connection.label: Trace and span evidence references
connection.description: The generic trace adapter publishes trace context and source references into the durable evidence stream.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Route deployment changes into durable intake
steps.content: Make change events available alongside observed symptoms so the investigator can test them as candidate causes.

connection.label: Deployment and change events
connection.description: Deployment events join the evidence stream with their source-provided identity and time.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Preserve source context in the event envelope
steps.content: Use a shared envelope for routing while retaining each signal's source-specific payload or reference. Only populate identifiers and timestamps that the source actually supplies.

decision.question: How should the intake path keep heterogeneous evidence joinable and auditable?
decision.chosen: Use a durable source-tagged envelope that preserves original event time and evidence references
decision.chosenReason: The correlation path needs comparable context without erasing source provenance or inventing fields that a source does not provide.

alternatives.option: Have each source call the investigator directly
alternatives.tradeoff: Reduces an intermediary but couples source availability and request latency to downstream analysis.

alternatives.option: Normalize every source into one lossy event shape
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies consumers but can discard trace, log, or deployment details needed to explain a hypothesis.

properties.purpose: Buffer a durable source-tagged envelope for metrics, logs, traces, and deployment changes. Preserve each source payload or evidence reference, source-provided event time, and available identity fields so downstream consumers can correlate and replay evidence without inventing missing metadata.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Correlate evidence in a stream processor
steps.content: Process the incoming evidence, associate events using source-provided service and trace context, and maintain anomaly and dependency updates without assuming a fixed collection interval.

component.label: Evidence Correlation Processor
component.description: Normalizes signal context and updates correlation state

properties.purpose: Consume durable evidence, preserve original timestamps and source references, correlate signals using available service and trace context, and emit investigation triggers and graph updates without assuming an event rate or time window.

component.highlightReason: Correlated time-series, multi-signal evidence, and graph updates feed automatic root-cause investigation.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Process evidence asynchronously
steps.content: Read the durable stream and checkpoint enough source context for retries or replay to produce explainable downstream state.

connection.label: Durable evidence events
connection.description: The processor consumes buffered source events and evidence references for normalization and correlation.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Store queryable time-series evidence
steps.content: Keep normalized signal context available for incident-window investigation while retaining links to original evidence. Choose physical retention and storage layout from the actual data policy and observed workload; neither is specified by the brief.

component.label: Signal Evidence Store
component.description: Time-series access to normalized signal context

properties.purpose: Store queryable time-series context and source references used by investigations, keeping original evidence retrievable and leaving retention and physical layout to measured workload and data policy.

component.highlightReason: Time-series access supports correlation of metrics, logs, traces, and deployment changes around a symptom.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Persist normalized signal context
steps.content: Write queryable evidence context from the correlator while preserving references that let the case view return to the original source records.

connection.label: Normalized time-series and evidence references
connection.description: Correlated signal context is persisted for investigations without replacing source evidence.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Represent service dependencies as a graph
steps.content: Use the existing graph database type to maintain the service dependency graph. Keep edge provenance available so graph propagation can be inspected against the trace or other source evidence that supports it.

component.label: Service Dependency Graph
component.description: Graph representation of service dependencies and provenance

properties.purpose: Maintain service dependency relationships derived from available topology and trace evidence, retaining provenance so graph traversal can be reviewed against its supporting observations.

component.highlightReason: The problem explicitly requires building and maintaining service dependency graphs and suggests graph-based propagation.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Update topology from observed evidence
steps.content: Feed graph updates from the correlation path so trace-derived dependencies and relevant changes can refresh the graph used by investigations.

connection.label: Observed dependency evidence
connection.description: Correlated trace and service context updates the maintained dependency graph with supporting provenance.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Keep graph propagation tied to its observations
steps.content: Choose a maintained graph projection with provenance rather than presenting an unexplained inferred dependency as ground truth.

decision.question: How should investigators inspect a dependency path used to propagate a symptom?
decision.chosen: Maintain graph relationships with the source evidence that supports each observed dependency
decision.chosenReason: The graph can support traversal while its provenance lets operators distinguish observed relationships from inferred ones.

alternatives.option: Rebuild a dependency graph separately for each request
alternatives.tradeoff: Keeps request logic self-contained but repeats work and makes graph state harder to compare across investigations.

alternatives.option: Store only an opaque topology score
alternatives.tradeoff: Can simplify ranking but hides the service path needed to inspect a causal chain.

properties.purpose: Maintain service dependency relationships from available topology and trace evidence. Retain the supporting source references and distinguish observed relationships from inferred propagation so an investigation can explain each traversed path.

steps.phase: 2. Ingest evidence and maintain service context
steps.title: Treat the graph as evidence, not a cause label
steps.content: A dependency path narrows which upstream services could explain a symptom; it does not establish that one of them failed. Combine graph traversal with metric, log, trace, and change evidence before ranking a root-cause hypothesis.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Create the investigation coordinator
steps.content: Use a backend service to open an investigation from a detected signal pattern or an operator request, fetch evidence, invoke the ranker, and store a reviewable result.

component.label: RCA Investigation Coordinator
component.description: Coordinates automatic investigations and operator requests

properties.purpose: Open investigations from correlation triggers or operator requests, retrieve signal, log, and topology evidence, call the causal ranker, preserve evidence links, and record results for operator review.

component.highlightReason: A coordinator joins automatic detection with evidence retrieval, cause ranking, and operator feedback.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Expose a consistent operator entry point
steps.content: Provide one API boundary for operator investigations and feedback, while keeping the automatic stream-triggered path inside the backend workflow.

component.label: RCA API Gateway
component.description: Operator API boundary for cases and feedback

properties.purpose: Route operator requests to inspect investigations and submit correctness feedback to the backend coordinator without coupling the console to internal evidence stores.

component.highlightReason: Monitoring and deployment systems integrate through ingestion, while operators need a bounded interface to review and correct results.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Give operators an evidence-first case view
steps.content: Show the ranked hypotheses together with the evidence and reasoning needed to inspect them, and collect an operator correction against the case.

component.label: Root Cause Review Console
component.description: Operator review of hypotheses, evidence, and correctness feedback

properties.purpose: Present ranked probable causes with their supporting metric, log, trace, topology, and change evidence, and let operators record whether a hypothesis was correct or provide a correction.

component.highlightReason: Evidence and reasoning for each hypothesis and operator feedback are both explicit requirements.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Serve causal hypothesis ranking
steps.content: Use the existing model-serving component for anomaly and causal inference, combining the stated hint families with graph propagation and returning ranked candidates that retain their evidence references.

component.label: Causal Hypothesis Ranker
component.description: Ranks probable causes from correlated signals and dependency evidence

properties.purpose: Analyze correlated time-series and graph context using causal inference and anomaly-detection approaches, then rank probable causes with evidence references and reasoning rather than presenting correlation as proof.

component.highlightReason: The existing model-serving catalog component can represent the causal inference and anomaly analysis service without adding a new component type.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Persist investigations and operator judgments
steps.content: Keep a case record containing the hypotheses shown, evidence references, relevant graph and model versions, and the operator's correctness feedback so later review and learning have context.

component.label: Investigation & Feedback Store
component.description: Case history, ranked hypotheses, evidence references, and feedback

properties.purpose: Persist investigation identity, ranked hypotheses, evidence references, the graph and model versions used, and operator correctness feedback for later inspection and offline learning.

component.highlightReason: Operator feedback must be associated with the hypotheses and evidence it evaluates.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Route operator review through the API
steps.content: The console requests case details and submits operator feedback through the same public API boundary.

connection.label: Case review and correctness feedback
connection.description: The operator console reads investigations and submits corrections through the RCA API.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Forward operator requests to the coordinator
steps.content: Keep the gateway thin and let the backend own investigation orchestration and case semantics.

connection.label: Investigation and feedback requests
connection.description: Operator case requests and correctness feedback are handled by the investigation coordinator.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Trigger investigations automatically
steps.content: A detected anomaly or correlated symptom can open an investigation without waiting for an operator to submit a request.

connection.label: Anomaly and investigation trigger
connection.description: The processor starts an RCA case when correlated signal evidence indicates an issue for investigation.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Retrieve time-series evidence for a case
steps.content: Fetch the signals relevant to the triggering symptom while retaining the source evidence links that will be shown with each hypothesis.

connection.label: Correlated signal evidence
connection.description: The coordinator retrieves time-series context and original evidence references for the investigation.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Retrieve relevant log records
steps.content: Use the log integration to resolve supporting log records rather than replacing them with a generated summary.

connection.label: Relevant log evidence
connection.description: The coordinator resolves log evidence for the case while preserving links back to source records.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Traverse the maintained service graph
steps.content: Retrieve dependency paths relevant to the symptom so propagation can contribute candidate causes and an inspectable explanation.

connection.label: Dependency paths and provenance
connection.description: The coordinator reads service relationships and their supporting evidence for graph-based propagation.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Rank candidates from multiple evidence families
steps.content: Pass correlated signal context, relevant topology, trace relationships, log evidence, and deployment changes to the causal ranker; return a bounded ranked list and its supporting evidence.

connection.label: Evidence-backed causal ranking request
connection.description: The ranker evaluates correlated signals and graph context and returns probable causes with evidence and reasoning.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Prefer a causal chain over proximity alone
steps.content: Use anomaly detection to find unusual signals, graph propagation to trace affected dependencies, and causal inference to rank explanations. Include deployment changes as possible causes but retain evidence that can distinguish a causal path from coincidence.

decision.question: What should make one probable cause rank above another?
decision.chosen: Rank with correlated anomalies, dependency propagation, causal inference, and deployment evidence, and return the supporting observations
decision.chosenReason: The prompt asks for causal chains and evidence, and its hints name these analysis families; a score without reasons would not meet that intent.

alternatives.option: Rank only by time proximity to the symptom
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple to compute but may mistake a coincident deployment or signal for a cause.

alternatives.option: Return an unranked list for operator triage
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids automated ranking but does not satisfy the stated scoring and ranking requirement.

properties.purpose: Analyze correlated time-series and graph context using causal inference and anomaly-detection approaches. Consider deployment changes as candidate evidence, rank probable causes, and return the observations and reasoning behind each result so operators can inspect correlation versus causation.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Record the hypotheses and evidence used
steps.content: Persist the returned ranking together with its evidence links and the versions of the model and graph used, making the result reproducible for review.

connection.label: Ranked hypotheses, evidence, and case state
connection.description: The case store retains the result and provenance needed for operator review and later feedback.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Return the reviewable case to the operator
steps.content: Return the ranked result through the operator API with links to the underlying observations and a clear indication that each item is a probable cause.

connection.label: Ranked case and evidence links
connection.description: The coordinator returns a reviewable investigation to the console through the API boundary.

steps.phase: 3. Produce and explain ranked root-cause hypotheses
steps.title: Show why each hypothesis is present
steps.content: For each ranked cause, show the supporting metric behavior, relevant log or trace references, the service path used for propagation, and any deployment change considered. Keep evidence links available so an operator can verify or correct the explanation.

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Evaluate and train from reviewed feedback
steps.content: Use the existing model-training component for offline analysis of operator corrections and reviewed incident outcomes, keeping training away from the investigation response path.

component.label: Offline RCA Evaluation & Training
component.description: Offline evaluation and learning from reviewed operator feedback

properties.purpose: Analyze reviewed operator correctness feedback and incident outcomes, evaluate candidate causal and anomaly models against evidence, and prepare candidates without changing the live investigation path.

component.highlightReason: The problem requires learning from operator feedback; offline evaluation keeps corrections auditable before they affect ranking.

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Track evaluated model versions
steps.content: Keep model candidates and the version used for each case distinguishable so an operator correction can be tied to the ranking that was actually shown.

component.label: RCA Model Registry
component.description: Versioned causal and anomaly models for reviewed promotion

properties.purpose: Track evaluated model versions and promotion state so investigations retain the model provenance used for ranking and a reviewed candidate can be selected for serving.

component.highlightReason: Version provenance links operator feedback to the model result and makes candidate promotion reviewable.

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Supply reviewed cases to offline evaluation
steps.content: Use the case record as the source of operator judgments and the evidence that was visible when each judgment was made.

connection.label: Reviewed outcomes and case evidence
connection.description: Offline evaluation reads operator feedback with the associated hypotheses, evidence, and model provenance.

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Register evaluated candidates
steps.content: Write candidate versions to the registry only after their evaluation and review evidence can be tied to the stated top-three target.

connection.label: Evaluated model candidate
connection.description: Offline evaluation supplies candidate model versions and their review context to the registry.

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Serve only the selected model version
steps.content: Make the reviewed model version available to the ranking service and retain the version identifier on each resulting case.

connection.label: Selected model version
connection.description: The registry supplies the selected evaluated model version to the serving component.

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Keep feedback from changing live rankings immediately
steps.content: Persist operator corrections with the case, evaluate them offline, and promote a model candidate through the registry after review. Do not treat a single correction as a verified cause or silently change the active ranking behavior.

decision.question: How should operator feedback influence future investigations?
decision.chosen: Use reviewed corrections in offline evaluation and promote model changes through the registry
decision.chosenReason: This preserves the evidence behind each label and allows candidate ranking to be checked against the stated accuracy target before serving it.

alternatives.option: Update the live model immediately after each correction
alternatives.tradeoff: Applies feedback quickly but can turn an unverified or ambiguous correction into an unstable cause label.
Preserves an audit trail but does not satisfy the requirement to learn from operator feedback.

properties.purpose: Use reviewed operator correctness feedback and incident outcomes for offline evaluation and candidate training. Keep each correction tied to its case evidence, evaluate candidates against the stated top-three accuracy target, and prepare a reviewed candidate for registry promotion without changing live ranking immediately.

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Validate the stated ingestion and diagnosis bounds
steps.content: Exercise both application and infrastructure evidence at the supplied scale and measure where the five-minute diagnosis bound is spent. Use observed payload sizes, source skew, event arrival, graph work, and model calls; do not add a burst multiplier or an unstated latency percentile.

scaleTrigger.metric: The stated 1TB+ of observability data daily, 100+ services with 1000+ metrics each, and root cause identification within 5 minutes
scaleTrigger.action: Run production-shaped ingestion and investigation checks with actual source distributions, locate queue, processing, storage, topology, and inference bottlenecks, then scale or partition the measured bottleneck while preserving evidence provenance
scaleTrigger.impact: Validates the supplied workload and diagnosis target without claiming a capacity number or a latency target beyond the problem statement

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Validate top-three quality with reviewed incidents
steps.content: Measure top-three suggested-cause accuracy on reviewed cases spanning both infrastructure and application issues. Define labeling and the denominator before interpreting the result, inspect whether evidence supports the ranked causes, and hold a candidate back when the stated target is not met.

scaleTrigger.metric: Accuracy above 80% for top-3 suggested causes
scaleTrigger.action: Compare ranked suggestions with reviewed incident outcomes, inspect incorrect or unsupported hypotheses, and use offline evaluation before promoting a candidate through the model registry
scaleTrigger.impact: Makes the stated ranking-quality target auditable while preserving evidence and operator review

steps.phase: 4. Learn from feedback and validate the stated targets
steps.title: Review the design against the original brief
steps.content: The architecture connects metrics, logs, traces, dependency topology, and deployment changes to an automatic evidence-backed ranking, exposes the reasoning to operators, and feeds reviewed corrections into offline learning. Treat the 5-minute, above-80% top-three, service/metric, and daily-data constraints as acceptance targets to demonstrate with measured workloads and reviewed cases; this walkthrough does not prove that the targets have been met.
